findings.claim: In EventManager (around line 118-119), mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, then `.integration` is read without a guard. When evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty this throws a TypeError, which breaks the Google Meet to Daily fallback.

In GoogleCalendarService createEvent() and updateEvent(), mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar. It is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or empty, which causes a null reference.
Several places destructure the first element of an array (`[first] = array`) and access its properties without guarding against undefined.
The optional chaining on `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` is redundant because mainHostDestinationCalendar is already checked in the ternary condition.

In GoogleCalendarService updateEvent (line ~256) and deleteEvent (line ~317), the fallback `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it never matches. As a result, updateEvent sends an undefined calendarId, and deleteEvent falls back to 'primary' instead of the booking's destination calendar.
In Google createEvent, selectedCalendar can be undefined when no destination calendar matches credentialId, but later code passes it directly as calendarId (e.g., calendar.events.patch).
Google createEvent picks the target calendar only by credentialId match, so destination calendars with a null credentialId go to 'primary' instead of the selected calendar.

In handleNewBooking (lines ~1063-1079), evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. Because of this, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op and all team members' destination calendars are dropped for collective events.

The organization slug condition in organizations/create.handler.ts (line ~151) is inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. With billing on, the org gets a slug before payment; with billing off, neither slug nor requestedSlug is set, causing NoOrganizationSlugError.

The loadUsers rewrite in handleNewBooking.ts changes behavior:
- An empty dynamicUserList throws a plain Error (500) instead of reaching the 404 path.
- Prisma errors are re-thrown as 400 with the raw message.
- Other errors are swallowed.
- The organization slug select is dropped while IsFixedAwareUser still declares it.

EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (lines ~338-380) loops over each destinationCalendar entry but passes the full event with all destination calendars to each integration, and does not forward externalId to the provider. Providers that read destinationCalendar[0] (Office365, Lark, CalDAV) therefore create every host's event on the first host's calendar.
LarkCalendarService (lines 128, 164, 192, 237) uses event.destinationCalendar[0], which targets the first calendar even in collective flows with multiple destination calendars and credentials.

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (Lark, Office365, packages/lib CalendarService) still declare createEvent(event) without credentialId. packages/lib CalendarService also selects only the first destination calendar at line 156.

Office365CalendarService updateEvent lacks the externalCalendarId parameter and deleteEvent lacks the event and externalCalendarId parameters required by the Calendar interface, so update and delete always use the default calendar path.

In EventManager updateAllCalendarEvents (lines ~511-542), credential can remain undefined when reference.credentialId points to a missing credential and the DB fallback finds nothing. updateEvent(credential, ...) is then called and throws, which turns the update into a failure result for every calendar in the booking.

The credential-from-DB fallback code is copy-pasted in three places (EventManager.ts:342-365, :515-538, handleCancelBooking.ts:431-441), and the copies have diverged. The handleCancelBooking copy lacks the app include and appName.

Video references (Zoom, Daily, etc.) no longer store credentialId because the expression changed to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. As a result, video meetings are not deleted when a booking is cancelled.
Team members are given hardcoded `firstName: ''` and `lastName: ''` (lines ~998-999), which the TeamMember type does not declare. This changes the team-member shape sent to emails and webhooks.

When cancelling a recurring booking, the series-delete block sits inside the per-reference loop but does not depend on the reference. It deletes the series N times using only the first calendar reference, so other hosts' copies are never deleted.

In handleCancelBooking lines 449-458, the code ignores the current reference and uses updBooking.references.find(). Each updated booking therefore contributes at most one _calendar reference, so only the first host's event is deleted. The branch also uses bookingToDelete.user.credentials, dropping a DB-fetched team credential.
The reschedule merge deletes only one old calendar event via .find, so other hosts' old copies remain.
Each team member's Google event is inserted with the main host as organizer and the same conferenceData requestId.
teamDestinationCalendars is populated through a side effect inside an async .map callback, which works only because the push runs before the first await.
In requestReschedule.handler.ts lines 240-242, the second optional chain in `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` is redundant inside the branch where bookingToReschedule is already checked.
No test covers the fan-out over multiple destination calendars, the reference credentialId/externalId mapping, or multi-reference update/cancel/reschedule.
schedulingType is added to CalendarEvent but nothing reads it; it only appears in webhook payloads.
A destination with no credentialId fans out to every organizer credential of that integration, duplicating events, and the resulting references lack externalCalendarId.
The updateAllCalendarEvents catch block no longer calls console.error(message), so failures are swallowed without logging and `message` is unused.

Two parameters redundantly carry the target calendar: EventManager passes externalId to CalendarManager.createEvent, which only echoes it back, and passes credentialId, which Google uses to search again.
Dynamic group bookings are not handled; the TODO was removed but the code only handles eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE'.
The user-visible calendar-note text at CalendarManager.ts:230 changed from 'organiser' to 'organizer'.
updateLocation saves calendar references with undefined externalCalendarId and credentialId because CalendarManager.updateEvent sets neither field.
The PR contains no-op edits such as `result.credentialId ?? undefined`, redundant length checks, and typed comparisons replaced with string literals.
The logic 'booking calendar else user calendar wrapped in array' is written two different ways across about 10 sites.
The public webhook payload's destinationCalendar changes from an object to an array, and is inconsistent: BOOKING_CREATED can send null while other triggers send [].
The organizer email on every host's Google event is destinationCalendar[0].externalId (the main host's calendar), even for other hosts' calendars.
In createAllCalendarEvents, the else branch (line ~380) calls createEvent(c, event) without passing destination.externalId, so externalCalendarId is undefined on that path.

coverage: pooled issues; severity and verdict are placeholders
